questions.q: What is a data stream in Data Cloud (Data 360)?
options: The configured connection that ingests a source object, with its category, key, and refresh mode
A finished dashboard that streams live charts to users
A saved segment of customers
The rule that decides which profiles are the same person
questions.explain: A data stream is the configured connection between a data source and Data 360. Identity resolution and segments are separate steps that come later.

questions.q: According to the New Data Stream wizard, which choices cannot be changed after the stream is saved?
options: The wizard's title and the stream's owner
The category and the field data types
Only the refresh schedule
Nothing; every setting can be edited freely later
questions.explain: The wizard warns that the category (Profile, Engagement, or Other) and the field data types cannot be changed after creation, so review them carefully.

questions.q: Where does ingested data land first?
options: Directly in a segment
In a data model object, already standardized
In a data lake object, roughly in the shape it arrived
In a CRM Analytics dataset
questions.explain: Raw ingested data is stored in a data lake object (DLO). Mapping to data model objects is a separate step.

questions.q: Why does field mapping matter so much to an analyst?
options: Mapping deletes duplicate records automatically
Mapping is only cosmetic and changes no behavior
Mapping speeds up the source system's own reports
Only mapped fields, or objects with relationships, can be used for segmentation and insights
questions.explain: Data 360 states that only mapped fields or objects with relationships are available for segmentation and insights, so an unmapped field is invisible downstream.

questions.q: A dashboard built on Data Cloud looks out of date. Where should you look first?
options: The stream's Refresh History for run status, mode, and record counts
The color palette of the dashboard
The Tableau Desktop installation
The user's browser bookmarks
questions.explain: Refresh History lists each run with its status and records processed, which tells you whether stale data is an ingestion problem.
